characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.043% P steel aged 10 h at 530°C shows modulated spinodal microstructure with carbon amplitude of 6.0 at.% and carbon-rich domains a few nm to ~15 nm long.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: carbon concentration maps (2–6 at.% C scale); 0.043% P steel aged 10 h at 530°C
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize spinodal decomposition / carbon partitioning during aging

characterization_methods.key_findings: High-P (0.043% P) steel exhibits SRO during quench and larger κ-carbide ordered domains than low-P steel.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe κ-carbide ordered domains / precipitation in high-P steel

characterization_methods.key_findings: Used with TEM and APT to study κ-carbide precipitation in the 0.043% P steel.
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm phase constitution / ordering in high-P aged steel

analytical_models.model_name: Phosphorus substitution for aluminum in κ-carbide

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted P substitution in κ-carbide reduces {100} cleavage stress by 45%, consistent with the observed notch-toughness reduction of aged high-P steels.

analytical_models.model_name: SRO kinetics of P and Al into κ-carbide corner positions during quenching
analytical_models.model_note: Thermodynamic preference of P for Al corner positions not included in the calculation.

parameters.name: relative SRO rate (P vs Al)
parameters.value: P SRO may be an order of magnitude faster than Al

computational_details.simulation_method: Random walk estimate of short-range ordering (SRO) kinetics

defect_interactions.interaction_type: phosphorus substitution in κ-carbide creating open-volume defects on {100}
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Phosphorus substitution for aluminum positions in κ-carbide is predicted to reduce the {100} cleavage stress by 45%.

interfaces.phase_evolution: short-range ordering (occurs during quench in high-P steel) → spinodal decomposition → coherent κ-carbide precipitation and coarsening.
interfaces.slip_behavior: planar slip and shear localization due to shearing of κ-carbide precipitates; {111} glide-plane decohesion at high strain rates.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent solution-treatment step for the cast high-P steel before 530°C aging (process definition lists proc_st-1050c-2h as parent).
Age hardening at 530°C for 10 h to precipitate nano-sized κ-carbide; this is the main process condition for this sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: DFT = J_Id (critical J integral near onset of stable crack growth)
measurement_conditions.test_standard: Schindler single-specimen method; ASTM E 1820; ASTM E 813

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic matrix with coherent nano-sized κ-carbide precipitates formed via spinodal decomposition and short-range ordering during 530°C aging; aged 10 h at 530°C.

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition (Table I, wt.%): Si 0.92, C 0.94, Mn 29.10, P 0.043, S 0.006, Mo 0.33, Al 8.28, Cu 0.09; Table IV refers to this heat as '0.94% Si, 0.043% P'.
After 10 h at 530°C, the APT carbon amplitude for the 0.043% P steel is 6.0 at.% (compared with 4.4 at.% for the 0.006% P steel).
The high-phosphorus (0.043% P) specimens exhibited short-range ordering (SRO) that took place during the quench and prior to spinodal decomposition.
Room-temperature Charpy V-notch impact energy for the 0.043% P steel aged 10 h at 530°C reads just above ~20 J/cm² from Figure 9 (no exact numeric labels printed).
Fracture of the aged 0.043% P, 0.94% Si specimen produced a dendritic pattern with cleavage along {100}.
The DFT of this sample (100 kJ/m²) is much lower than the 1.07% Si low-P specimens aged for similar times at 530°C (376 kJ/m²).
In the 530°C age-hardening curve (Fig. 2b, '1% Si' steel), the 0.043% P steel attains peak hardness near 380 BHN around 30 h.
